attempts.summary: On node1, /srv/data is now backed by a loopback-mounted Btrfs filesystem (no LVM/native-snapshot fs was available on the ext4 root), managed by a systemd oneshot unit (srv-data-btrfs.service) that reattaches the loop device and mounts the top-level subvolume plus the /data subvolume at boot. Application data was populated, a read-only Btrfs snapshot was taken as a baseline, the live directory was then modified (file corrupted, file deleted, extraneous file added), and the directory was restored via rsync --delete from the snapshot back to an exact byte-for-byte match of the baseline (verified by sha256). The node was then restarted using systemctl reboot; boot_id changed confirming a real restart, the mount service came back active/enabled automatically, the btrfs subvolumes (data + snapshot) survived, and /srv/data content was re-verified as byte-identical to the pre-restart baseline and to the snapshot subvolume.
